slides.headline: She became the first woman CEO in U.S. Bancorp's 160-year history.
Gunjan Kedia
slides.body: Kedia had already spent years rising through U.S. Bancorp's leadership, most recently as President - the bank's second-highest role - before the board named her Chief Executive Officer, effective at the close of the April 2025 annual shareholder meeting.

slides.headline: No woman had led the bank before - in over 160 years.
slides.body: U.S. Bancorp, one of the largest regional banks in the United States, had never had a female CEO since its founding. Kedia also joined the company's Board of Directors alongside taking the role.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: Indian-origin leadership at the top of American finance isn't new anymore.
slides.body: From tech to banking, Indian-origin executives now run some of the largest companies in the world. Each one that breaks a barrier that specific company held for over a century makes the next one less remarkable, and more expected.
